Title: Register with email
User story: As a Customer, I want to create an account using email and password so that I can access care services.
Acceptance criteria: Validate email, 10–72-character password and matching confirmation; send only email, unchanged password and accountType CUSTOMER; registration alone does not create an authenticated session.

Title: Verify my email
User story: As a Customer, I want to verify my email with a code so that my account can be authenticated.
Acceptance criteria: Accept exactly six digits including leading zeroes, paste and OTP autofill; authenticate only after successful verification, secure persistence and active CUSTOMER validation; invalid/expired codes remain retryable.

Title: Resend or resume email verification
User story: As a Customer, I want to request another email code or resume a pending verification so that I can finish registration later.
Acceptance criteria: Support existing-email verification without registering again; honor cooldown and longer server Retry-After; changing email clears the draft OTP; generic responses do not reveal account existence.

Title: Sign in with password
User story: As a Customer, I want to sign in with email or username and password so that I can return to my account.
Acceptance criteria: POST identifier with trimmed email/username and unchanged password; reject wrong role/inactive account; persist the validated session and load confirmed profile state before entry routing.

Title: Request phone registration or sign-in
User story: As a Customer, I want to enter my international mobile number so that I can register or sign in without a password.
Acceptance criteria: Validate E.164 and send phoneNumber/accountType CUSTOMER to the public OTP request endpoint; no email/password is required; accepted OTP request does not itself authenticate or prove account creation.

Title: Verify my phone
User story: As a Customer, I want to verify an SMS code so that I can securely access my phone-based account.
Acceptance criteria: Send phoneNumber, six-digit string OTP and CUSTOMER; permit null email in a valid phone-only account; support invalid-code retry, resend cooldown and changing number without creating a separate email registration.

Title: See verification success
User story: As a Customer, I want a clear email or phone verification confirmation so that I understand registration/sign-in succeeded.
Acceptance criteria: Show the appropriate wording and supplied one-shot animation only after secure authenticated success; support reduced motion; Continue follows profile/market routing; restart/logout does not replay stale success.

Title: Restore and refresh my session
User story: As a Customer, I want to reopen the app securely without unnecessary sign-in so that I can continue my journey.
Acceptance criteria: Read secure session and current user; serialize refresh and persist both rotated tokens; clear invalid credentials and show recoverable network failures accurately; restored sessions do not replay verification success.

Title: Sign out of this or every session
User story: As a Customer, I want to sign out of one or all sessions so that I can control account access.
Acceptance criteria: Use the documented logout and logout-all operations; clear local credentials only through the current confirmed success policy; failed logout remains a visible retryable error; clear per-user market/catalog state on sign-out.

Title: Sign in with Google
User story: As a Customer, I want to use Google identity so that I can access my account with fewer credentials.
Acceptance criteria: Obtain a Google ID token and send accountType CUSTOMER; validate returned active role/session; handle cancellation and missing platform/backend client configuration without fake success. Backend deployment/configuration must be verified before activation.

Title: Link a phone to my email account
User story: As an email-registered Customer, I want to add and verify a mobile number on the same account so that my contact details remain unified.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm authenticated linking/update endpoints, uniqueness and OTP rules; verify account identity is retained; never use standalone phone sign-in as an assumed account-linking operation.

Title: Reset my password
User story: As a Customer, I want to reset a forgotten password so that I can recover account access.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm recovery request/verification/password-change contracts and expiry rules; use non-enumerating responses and safe retries; keep the current unsupported action disabled rather than inventing a reset route.

Title: Sign in with Apple
User story: As a Customer, I want to use Apple identity so that I can access my account with an approved alternative identity method.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm Apple token exchange, account matching, platform configuration and role validation; handle cancellation and private relay addresses correctly under the confirmed contract; do not present the disabled Apple button as implemented sign-in.

Title: Create my customer profile
User story: As a Customer, I want to enter my name and address in one form so that the app can personalize my experience.
Acceptance criteria: Require first/last name, address line 1, city and country; allow documented optional address/photo fields; submit exactly the ten profile DTO fields with no DOB, gender, NIC, IDs or completion flags.

Title: Restore and edit my profile
User story: As a Customer, I want my saved details restored when editing so that I can update them without losing other information.
Acceptance criteria: Use the documented profile GET; only its confirmed 404 opens creation; preserve optional fields under full-replacement PUT and retain edits after failed save; unknown failures remain errors.

Title: Select, upload, preview and remove my photo
User story: As a Customer, I want to preview and change an optional profile photo so that I can recognize my account.
Acceptance criteria: Accept JPG/PNG/WebP within 10 MB; upload one binary file part and display the photo only from the returned server URL; show remote loading/error/retry without a selected-file fallback; remove clears the photo and profile submission uses only the returned URL.

Title: View my uploaded photo after reopening
User story: As a Customer, I want my saved photo to load from its server URL so that it remains visible beyond the current form.
Acceptance criteria: The documented public URL must return a decodable image without app Authorization; expose retry and visible failure rather than silent replacement; resolve the observed 403 and verify reopening and URL-only display after server access is corrected.

Title: Continue with the sole available market
User story: As a Customer, I want the only available market selected automatically so that I do not make an unnecessary choice.
Acceptance criteria: Fetch active markets, select the single returned active market, display its country/currency/timezone and offer Continue; empty/error results never enable an invented market.

Title: Choose among multiple markets
User story: As a Customer, I want to select my desired market so that I see relevant services.
Acceptance criteria: Offer returned active markets in a dropdown; suggest only a unique saved-country match with an explanation; disable Continue until valid selection; retain selected market in current app state without an invented server PUT.

Title: Change market from Home
User story: As a Customer, I want to change markets later so that I can arrange care in another supported market.
Acceptance criteria: Keep the committed market until Continue; clear stale services on change and request the chosen ID; ignore late responses from a previous market; logout clears in-memory state; the account/environment-scoped device preference restores after restart only when the market remains active.

Title: Suggest a market from actual location
User story: As a Customer, I want a location-based market suggestion so that I can choose the appropriate area faster.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm point-to-market boundaries/resolver and location/geocoding policy; request permission transparently and preserve manual selection when denied; never equate device locale or saved country with actual GPS location.

Title: Browse services in my market
User story: As a Customer, I want a visual catalog for my market so that I can find relevant care services.
Acceptance criteria: Send the selected returned marketId; show real names/descriptions and optional cover/icon media; show distinct loading, empty and retry states; no sample services are inserted into production.

Title: Search the service catalog
User story: As a Customer, I want to search services so that I can quickly find the care I need.
Acceptance criteria: Filter the currently returned unpaginated list by name/description; distinguish no matches from no market services; clearing search restores the list without fabricating server-side search results.

Title: Understand service access status
User story: As a Customer, I want access badges and reasons so that I know whether I can proceed or must provide more information.
Acceptance criteria: Distinguish all documented statuses, including restricted/rejected/review/option checks; restricted services stay visible; show returned reasons and handle unknown statuses conservatively rather than labeling them Available.

Title: Select a service option
User story: As a Customer, I want to choose an available option within a service so that I can request the correct type of care.
Acceptance criteria: Read options using service.id as serviceTypeId plus marketId; use option-specific access and descriptions; handle no options/errors and preserve selected service/option context.

Title: Read booking context and responsibilities
User story: As a Customer, I want to understand the selected option's rules and responsibilities so that I can prepare a valid request.
Acceptance criteria: Fetch context with market/service/option IDs; render returned delivery modes, scheduling model and responsibilities; use bookingSchema rather than provider setup fields; invalidate context after selection changes.

Title: Complete configured personal requirements
User story: As a Customer, I want forms built from applicable requirements so that I can become eligible for my chosen service.
Acceptance criteria: Load GLOBAL/SERVICE/OPTION requirements for the selection; render configured types, choices and requiredness; do not add DOB/NIC/gender to the Customer profile DTO or ask for Provider-only setup fields.

Title: Save and restore reusable answers
User story: As a Customer, I want saved answers reused so that I do not repeatedly provide the same information.
Acceptance criteria: Restore existing submissions and preserve JSON value types; batch-save requirementId/value/optional expiry only; omitted answers follow documented preservation semantics; retain draft after failure.

Title: Upload private evidence
User story: As a Customer, I want to attach identity or supporting documents securely so that required evidence can be reviewed.
Acceptance criteria: Use the private document uploader, not public profile images; enforce endpoint and field count/type/size limits; submit returned keys in files arrays, never s3 URLs or local paths; handle 413 and partial workflow failure.

Title: View my private evidence
User story: As a Customer, I want to preview my uploaded evidence so that I can confirm I attached the correct file.
Acceptance criteria: Request a view URL for the owned returned key; honor signed URL expiry and request a fresh URL when needed; never expose private URLs/tokens in logs or treat a missing upload as approved evidence.

Title: Track requirement review and correct rejection
User story: As a Customer, I want review statuses and rejection reasons so that I know what to correct before booking.
Acceptance criteria: Distinguish missing/provided/pending/approved/rejected/expired from returned submissions; allow documented answer/evidence replacement; replacing evidence can reset dependent approval; never locally grant approval.

Title: Return to my service after requirements
User story: As a Customer, I want to continue the same service journey after providing details so that I do not restart my selection.
Acceptance criteria: Retain market/service/option and a return destination; recheck eligibility after submission, resume or explicit refresh; pending review remains pending and unknown reason codes display server guidance safely.

Title: Choose delivery and time
User story: As a Customer, I want a supported delivery mode and future time window so that I can request care when and where needed.
Acceptance criteria: Offer only returned modes; validate future time/range in market timezone; distinguish TIME_BASED from ROUTE_BASED; preserve correct offset-aware search timestamps and market-local booking timestamps.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: Provide a physical location
User story: As a Customer, I want to supply a meeting location so that travelling providers can assess my request.
Acceptance criteria: Request foreground location permission only when needed and allow manual entry if denied; validate coordinates/address; ONLINE needs no coordinates; map/geocoding provider configuration is a frontend prerequisite.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: Provide route-based search details
User story: As a Customer, I want to specify route endpoints and time so that route-based services can be searched correctly.
Acceptance criteria: Use the documented route-based search shape and required points; do not send mutually incompatible time-based fields; recalculate/reset results when route/time changes and do not claim live road ETA.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: Filter and search available providers
User story: As a Customer, I want providers matching my exact option, schedule and preferences so that I can choose suitable care.
Acceptance criteria: Submit documented provider-search fields and language/approved-skill preferences; use exact selected market/service/option/mode; handle no results with change-time/location actions; ignore stale in-flight results.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: Browse candidates and pagination
User story: As a Customer, I want provider summaries and more results so that I can compare suitable candidates.
Acceptance criteria: Show returned provider identity/photo/rating/skills with null-safe fallbacks; reset pagination when context changes; retain provider entity IDs and location IDs, not assignment/user IDs; no fabricated ratings or prices.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: Interpret service locations correctly
User story: As a Customer, I want accurate candidate location information so that I understand where care is offered.
Acceptance criteria: Distinguish fixed business locations from approximate travelling-provider coverage centres; retain candidate providerLocationId where required; never label a coverage pin as a live provider position.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: Select one provider or a compatible team
User story: As a Customer, I want the required number of compatible providers so that the service is properly staffed.
Acceptance criteria: Follow returned fulfillment/count rules; require distinct provider entities; multiple locations for one provider do not form a team; preserve selected location/context compatibility.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: Answer booking-specific questions
User story: As a Customer, I want to answer only applicable booking questions so that my request includes the necessary care details.
Acceptance criteria: Render common and selected-option bookingSchema fields; preserve typed values/choice IDs; support only documented conditions and clear hidden dependent answers; keep booking answers separate from reusable requirements.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: Review and submit a booking
User story: As a Customer, I want to review my complete request before submitting so that I can confirm the correct care arrangement.
Acceptance criteria: Summarize actual selection/time/location/providers/answers and allowed payment method; send the documented booking DTO without price/status overrides; honor server revalidation of eligibility, coverage, schedules and capacity.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: Recover safely from uncertain submission
User story: As a Customer, I want clear guidance after a booking timeout so that I do not accidentally create duplicate requests.
Acceptance criteria: Do not blindly auto-replay booking POST or invent an idempotency contract; explain uncertain outcome and refresh the documented owned booking list for inspection; surface unresolved ambiguity rather than claiming success or absence.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: View my bookings
User story: As a Customer, I want to view my submitted bookings so that I can follow my care requests.
Acceptance criteria: Read the owned booking array in backend order; show returned job/payment information and empty/error states; a detail view may use a returned list record but must not call an invented single-booking endpoint.

Epic: Customer scheduling, provider search and booking
Title: Cancel or modify a booking
User story: As a Customer, I want to request supported booking changes so that I can respond when my plans change.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm cancellation/modification endpoints, permitted states, ownership and financial consequences; do not expose a successful cancellation action against an unsupported route.

Title: Discover enabled payment capabilities
User story: As a Customer, I want only supported payment actions shown so that I do not attempt unavailable transactions.
Acceptance criteria: Read payment-settings/capabilities on entry/resume and after relevant 503 responses; intersect capabilities with the selected option's allowed methods; never offer a gateway selector or admin settings access.

Title: Create and view currency wallets
User story: As a Customer, I want wallet balances in supported currencies so that I can understand available funds.
Acceptance criteria: Use documented wallet create/read/list operations; show available/reserved/pending and fundingMode separately; distinguish missing wallet from empty history; use decimal-safe amounts and authoritative server balances.

Title: Review wallet transaction history
User story: As a Customer, I want paginated wallet activity so that I can understand credits, debits and holds.
Acceptance criteria: Read Spring Page content/metadata; show backend transaction values/currency; validate paging bounds and handle empty/error pages without calculating an authoritative balance from displayed entries.

Title: Set up and list payment methods
User story: As a Customer, I want to manage supported card/bank instruments so that enabled wallet actions have a valid method.
Acceptance criteria: Respect cardLinking/bankLinking flags; use documented setup/list operations; label VERIFIED_MOCK/test instruments honestly and do not imply real card verification or invent edit/delete endpoints.

Title: Top up a wallet
User story: As a Customer, I want to initiate a permitted top-up so that I can fund a wallet booking.
Acceptance criteria: Validate amount/currency/method and reuse the same idempotency key for the same attempt; retain intentId and read real backend outcome; refresh balance after confirmed success; test-mode actions remain clearly simulated.

Title: Withdraw supported available funds
User story: As a Customer, I want an enabled withdrawal flow so that I can request available wallet funds back.
Acceptance criteria: Require capabilities and an eligible owned bank method; use the documented idempotency key and intent handling; distinguish reserved/pending funds from withdrawable funds; current MOCK never claims a real bank payout.

Title: Reserve wallet funds for a booking
User story: As a Customer, I want to pay an eligible booking with wallet funds so that its amount is reserved safely.
Acceptance criteria: Use the owned booking wallet-payment endpoint with no client amount override; display RESERVED as a hold, not final settlement; insufficient funds offers top-up and retry of the same booking without duplicate reservation.

Title: Initiate card payment for a booking
User story: As a Customer, I want to start a supported card payment so that I can complete an eligible card booking.
Acceptance criteria: Intersect cardCheckout with option CARD support; create the documented idempotent session and retain intentId; do not invent hosted checkout URLs or send card data to the current mock session; PENDING is not paid.

Title: Recheck payment outcomes and balance integrity
User story: As a Customer, I want reliable payment status after interruptions so that I do not repeat charges or trust an incorrect balance.
Acceptance criteria: Read retained owned intents after timeout/resume; handle documented terminal/refund/conflict states without assuming automatic refunds; block further actions when reconciliation is unbalanced and report the issue rather than repairing balances locally.

Title: Use production card processing and refunds
User story: As a Customer, I want real verified payment processing so that actual payments and supported refunds can be completed securely.
Acceptance criteria: Require configured gateway, hosted/tokenization flow, verified callbacks and finance/refund contracts; never send simulated SUCCESS events as proof of a real payment; PAID does not mean provider settlement.

Title: Register a provider account
User story: As a Provider, I want to register with email/password so that I can apply to offer services.
Acceptance criteria: Validate required registration fields/confirmation and local agreement control; send SERVICE_PROVIDER identity through the confirmed contract; do not authenticate from registration alone or send UI-only agreement/confirmation fields without a contract.

Title: Verify email and resend a code
User story: As a Provider, I want to verify my email and request a replacement code so that I can activate my sign-in journey.
Acceptance criteria: Preserve six-digit codes and verified email context; handle invalid/expired code, cooldown and resend failures; validate SERVICE_PROVIDER session before entering onboarding.

Title: Sign in with password
User story: As a Provider, I want to sign in using email or username so that I can manage my services.
Acceptance criteria: POST /auth/login sends identifier and unchanged password, not username as a payload key; require SERVICE_PROVIDER role, expiry checks and secure persistence; keep readable validation/network errors.

Title: Restore and refresh my session
User story: As a Provider, I want a secure restored session so that I can return to incomplete or registered services.
Acceptance criteria: Handle expired sessions through documented token rotation with single-flight refresh; protect routes by session and entry gate; late refresh cannot restore a signed-out account.

Title: Sign out safely
User story: As a Provider, I want to sign out even when the network is unavailable so that local access to my account can be removed.
Acceptance criteria: Attempt server logout using the current documented refresh-token contract; current Provider policy permits local clear after server/network failure; redirect only after secure clear succeeds and retain a safe error if local clearing fails.

Title: Activate Google sign-in
User story: As a Provider, I want to use Google identity so that I can access the provider app conveniently.
Acceptance criteria: Reconnect the dormant implemented identity/controller path only after client/backend configuration validation; handle cancellation and role/session checks; disabled social buttons do not count as an active feature.

Title: Register or sign in with phone
User story: As a Provider, I want a supported phone OTP entry method so that I can access the Provider app without email/password.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm Provider-specific accountType, linking and OTP/session behavior before connecting a Provider UI; preserve SERVICE_PROVIDER validation and nullable identity fields; the Customer phone screen does not count as a Provider implementation.

Title: Reset my provider password
User story: As a Provider, I want a supported password-reset flow so that I can recover access to my account.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm reset initiation, verification, password and rate-limit contracts; preserve generic account-existence responses; keep unsupported actions explanatory until they are connected.

Title: Sign in with Apple
User story: As a Provider, I want a supported Apple identity option so that I can use my preferred sign-in method.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm Provider role/token exchange, account matching and native configuration; handle cancellation and relay email without guessed account linking; dormant Google code does not implement Apple sign-in.

Title: Complete provider details and market
User story: As a Provider, I want to provide my personal details and market so that I meet account prerequisites for service registration.
Acceptance criteria: Use confirmed name/DOB/gender/market/availability fields; offer MALE and FEMALE with exact uppercase wire values; validate market and dates; optional values are preserved according to Provider PUT semantics.

Title: Restore and edit provider details
User story: As a Provider, I want saved profile details restored when editing so that I do not lose existing information.
Acceptance criteria: Read the current confirmed GET profile implementation; preserve optional NIC/passport/photo fields on full-profile edits; use completion state for onboarding routing rather than treating arbitrary profile HTTP errors as missing data.

Title: Set my work availability status
User story: As a Provider, I want to change whether I am available for work so that my account reflects my current availability.
Acceptance criteria: Update documented AVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE/OFFLINE values using the current profile flow with other fields preserved; confirm server result before presenting saved state; do not equate OFFLINE with every future appointment being unavailable.

Title: See the right first-use dashboard
User story: As a Provider, I want Home to reflect whether I have registered services so that the next action is relevant.
Acceptance criteria: A confirmed empty assignment list shows first-service invitation; existing pending/rejected/incomplete services still use the registered variant; loading/failure does not masquerade as a new provider.

Title: Review my registered services
User story: As a Provider, I want service status and selected sub-services on Home so that I can resume the correct setup or review screen.
Acceptance criteria: Use actual assignments/options/completion data and current status precedence; route pending/rejected services to status/correction and incomplete setup to the proper flow; refresh after relevant edits and return/resume.

Title: Explore the service catalog
User story: As a Provider, I want to browse services I can offer so that I can select the right registration opportunity.
Acceptance criteria: Load real catalog IDs and descriptions; distinguish registered and available services/statuses; categories absent from the catalog fall back to browsing rather than using fabricated IDs; retain loading/empty/retry states.

Title: Inspect approved sub-service information
User story: As a Provider, I want to inspect an approved sub-service profile so that I understand the information published for that service.
Acceptance criteria: Load the actual selected option and saved related data; guard against inactive/unapproved options and route safely; show current locations, schedule and details without assuming approval from a local draft.

Title: View activity/community metrics and resources
User story: As a Provider, I want real business metrics and resource content so that I can understand and improve my activity.
Acceptance criteria: Retain honest unavailable placeholders until Provider-authorized metrics/content contracts exist; distinguish unknown from zero; never call Super Admin dashboard APIs for Provider data or fabricate counts/resources.

Title: Register one or more main services
User story: As a Provider, I want to choose main services so that I can offer multiple types of work.
Acceptance criteria: Resolve actual catalog IDs and existing assignments; register main services sequentially using the documented POST; recover an existing assignment before retry and do not accidentally replace unrelated assignments.

Title: Load service-specific setup requirements
User story: As a Provider, I want setup driven by the selected service so that I provide only applicable details.
Acceptance criteria: Read schema and public options plus existing registration; honor enabled/disabled/optional/required sections and documented constraints; unsupported/malformed metadata must not be silently considered complete.

Title: Select sub-services/options
User story: As a Provider, I want to choose offered sub-services so that customers can request my supported options.
Acceptance criteria: Restore actual selected option IDs; apply backend minimum/maximum/membership rules; send exact optionIds using assignment context and preserve draft/error state if saving fails.

Title: Provide experience and basic service details
User story: As a Provider, I want to enter required experience and service information so that my application accurately represents my offering.
Acceptance criteria: Use documented numeric assignment experience and applicable option/common fields; validate configured requirements; distinguish assignment-level values from option details and preserve saved values during unrelated edits.

Title: Select supported languages
User story: As a Provider, I want to record languages for a service assignment so that compatible customers can find me.
Acceptance criteria: Use ENGLISH/SINHALA/TAMIL only; restore saved selection and skip unchanged writes; after uncertain 5xx/transport error continue only if read-back confirms the exact set; verify resolution of the historically observed language PUT 500 before live acceptance.

Title: Select service skills
User story: As a Provider, I want to select catalog skills so that my service application includes relevant capabilities.
Acceptance criteria: Persist unique catalog skillIds in assignment scope; preserve identity when different skills share a label; reflect returned review state and do not represent assignment skills as editable global profile skills.

Title: Configure weekly availability
User story: As a Provider, I want to set service working days and hours so that matching considers my schedule.
Acceptance criteria: Use documented availableAnyDay/availableAnyTime/weeklySlots values and valid time ranges; restore saved days/times; saving unrelated information does not reset the schedule; do not write assignment hours as global hours.

Title: Manage unavailable dates
User story: As a Provider, I want to mark exception dates so that I am not matched when I cannot work.
Acceptance criteria: List/add/remove dates using returned IDs and documented operations; validate dates/duplicates as contracted; refresh actual saved state after mutation and preserve errors/drafts accurately.

Title: Select supported delivery modes and service areas
User story: As a Provider, I want to define where each option is delivered so that customers are matched to the correct coverage or business location.
Acceptance criteria: Use assignment/option/delivery-mode context; require coordinates and positive radius for provider visits, null radius for customer visits, and omit areas for ONLINE; persist the documented direct area array and restore existing values.

Title: Choose a map location with permission fallback
User story: As a Provider, I want map search, a pin and optional current location so that I can enter service coverage accurately.
Acceptance criteria: Preserve existing saved pin; request foreground permission and permit address/manual fallback after denial, GPS failure or unavailable map; support radius preview; Google Maps/geocoding platform configuration must be validated for release.

Title: Complete dynamic service fields
User story: As a Provider, I want fields based on the service schema so that I can provide all applicable service information.
Acceptance criteria: Render configured common and selected-option types while preserving JSON values; shared optionIds fields appear once; enforce choices/limits/requiredness and supported conditions; unsupported structures fail visibly.

Title: Reuse approved inherited answers
User story: As a Provider, I want eligible answers reused across configured scopes so that I do not repeat already approved information.
Acceptance criteria: Retain backend reuseScope/reused metadata and inherited values; do not overwrite approved inherited answers with empty draft defaults; editing follows the documented submission/review flow rather than local approval.

Title: Save and resume service drafts
User story: As a Provider, I want incomplete registration retained securely so that I can finish later without losing valid work.
Acceptance criteria: Encrypt drafts and scope them by account/service; merge server values without allowing empty stale drafts to erase saved state; preserve pending edits after failure and prevent cross-account restoration.

Title: View applicable document requirements
User story: As a Provider, I want required documents matched to my selected service/options so that I upload the correct evidence.
Acceptance criteria: Include common and selected-option requirements only; match existing documents by documentTypeId; show returned type/name, review and expiry information without invented review fields.

Title: Upload and register a required document
User story: As a Provider, I want to upload a valid document with its metadata so that my application can be reviewed.
Acceptance criteria: Enforce PDF/JPG/PNG/WebP and documented endpoint/field limits; upload binary first then register returned key and required metadata; retain file/draft on failure and prevent duplicate registration during retry.

Title: Preview existing private documents
User story: As a Provider, I want to view my uploaded documents so that I can confirm their correctness.
Acceptance criteria: Use bounded session previews for recent images and documented signed view URLs for existing private keys; refresh expired viewing URLs; never treat s3 URLs as a public viewer or expose signed URLs in diagnostics.

Title: Replace or delete a document
User story: As a Provider, I want to correct an attachment so that outdated or rejected evidence can be replaced.
Acceptance criteria: Use the current documented replacement/deletion workflow and returned document IDs; preserve old valid record until the contracted mutation succeeds; display the refreshed backend review result rather than keeping prior approval.

Title: Track review, expiry and rejection
User story: As a Provider, I want clear document statuses and rejection reasons so that I know what action is required.
Acceptance criteria: Distinguish pending/approved/rejected/expired/missing from actual review/expiry data; show rejectionReason safely; do not invent grace periods or countdowns from createdAt.

Title: Add certificates
User story: As a Provider, I want to attach service certificates so that relevant qualifications can be reviewed.
Acceptance criteria: Upload evidence before the documented metadata POST; show existing records/review state; check returned key/records before retry to avoid duplicates; do not invent certificate update/delete operations.

Title: Add education records
User story: As a Provider, I want to provide required education evidence so that my application meets service standards.
Acceptance criteria: Render only enabled requirements and documented fields; upload first and create the record through its confirmed contract; restore existing review state and preserve input after error without unsupported mutations.

Title: Review and finish service registration
User story: As a Provider, I want to review all saved service information so that I can finish a complete application.
Acceptance criteria: Review/edit actual service sections; reread saved requirements/documents and server completion before advancement; do not replay already saved replacements or invent a submit-application endpoint; pending review is not approval.
Dependencies: P-REG-04, P-REG-05, P-REG-06, P-REG-07, P-REG-09, P-REG-11, P-DOC-02

Title: Track application status
User story: As a Provider, I want to see incomplete, pending, approved, rejected or inactive application status so that I know whether I can offer the service.
Acceptance criteria: Derive status from actual assignment/completion/option review data; preserve option-level pending/rejected details even when aggregate state differs; refresh after edits, resume and explicit refresh, with safe read-error recovery.

Title: Correct and resubmit rejected information
User story: As a Provider, I want rejection reasons linked to their editors so that I can fix the exact issue.
Acceptance criteria: Open the first applicable correction/document editor; preserve unaffected saved details; refresh server recalculated verification after save and label re-upload only when actual returned state/key matches successful replacement history.

Title: View my account/profile overview
User story: As a Provider, I want my confirmed profile and account information together so that I can understand my verification and service setup.
Acceptance criteria: Use current session/profile/completion/assignment/document sources; show returned ratings/counts only when available; missing optional values and read failures remain honest unavailable/error states.

Title: Manage account-wide skills and languages
User story: As a Provider, I want global skills/languages so that my account preferences can be managed independently of a service assignment.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm global read/write/catalog and inheritance contracts; connect existing editor UI only to those confirmed endpoints; assignment-scoped skills/languages must not silently implement a global setting.

Title: Manage account-wide working hours
User story: As a Provider, I want global working hours so that I can control my default schedule across services.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm global slots/timezone and interaction with assignment schedules; connect the existing editor only after contract validation; preserve stored values and never label an unsent edit as saved.

Title: Manage payout account details
User story: As a Provider, I want verified payout details so that supported earnings payouts use the correct destination.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm global payout/profile and bank catalog/verification contracts or explicitly redesign around documented payment-method APIs; preserve masked reads and never submit an unchanged mask as a real account number; mock bank setup is not a real payout destination.

Title: Upload a provider profile photo
User story: As a Provider, I want to upload/change my photo so that my public profile is recognizable.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm the Provider upload role/type/limit and durable URL/key contract before connecting a picker; preserve current saved photo during unrelated PUTs; do not assume Customer-specific uploader rules apply unchanged.

Title: Update my personal address
User story: As a Provider, I want to update my residential address so that my personal information remains current.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm residential address read/write fields and validation; a business market or service area is not a residential address; preserve unrelated profile data and expose read/write failures honestly.

Title: View completed-booking and business metrics
User story: As a Provider, I want accurate account-wide performance statistics so that I can monitor my work.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm Provider-owned counters and counted statuses; distinguish unavailable/error from zero; never derive unsupported completed-booking counts from service registrations or Admin-only statistics.

Title: Change verified email or phone
User story: As a Provider, I want supported contact-change verification so that I can update how the platform reaches me.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm authenticated contact read/update, uniqueness and verification contracts; displaying session email/phone does not authorize changing them through profile PUT; retain the same account and prevent accidental account creation/linking.

Title: Browse my opportunities
User story: As a Provider, I want eligible incoming opportunities so that I can decide which work to consider.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm Provider request/list ownership, visibility, filtering and paging contracts; show real empty/error states and backend eligible requests; a placeholder route is not an operational inbox.

Title: Review an assigned/requested job
User story: As a Provider, I want permitted job details so that I can assess the care request responsibly.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm Provider-owned detail fields, customer-contact visibility, schedule/location and payment information; reject unauthorized jobs; do not reuse Customer detail assumptions or expose private customer evidence without authority.

Title: Accept or decline work
User story: As a Provider, I want to accept or decline an eligible request so that my work commitments are explicit.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm transitions, timeout/expiry, concurrency and conflict contracts; success must be server-confirmed; prevent duplicate acceptance and do not invent automatic OPEN_REQUEST dispatch/offer behavior.

Title: Manage an active job lifecycle
User story: As a Provider, I want supported start/completion/cancellation actions so that actual work progress can be recorded.
Acceptance criteria: Define allowed states, authorization, evidence/dispute requirements and financial consequences; no locally advanced job or settlement status; expose only confirmed operations.

Title: View my work calendar
User story: As a Provider, I want a calendar of confirmed work so that I can plan my time and avoid conflicts.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm Provider bookings/calendar source and market timezone rules; distinguish recurring availability from actual booked jobs; use server conflict checks rather than a local calendar as booking authority.

Title: Exchange permitted job messages
User story: As a Provider, I want authorized conversations with customers so that I can coordinate agreed care.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm conversation membership, message/read/attachment APIs and moderation/privacy rules; maintain retry/order/unread semantics; do not label the current Messages placeholder as functional chat.

Title: View wallet balances and history
User story: As a Provider, I want my supported currency wallets and ledger history so that I can understand available, held and pending funds.
Acceptance criteria: Use owned /me wallet/list/read/history contracts with decimal-safe amounts and pagination; distinguish pending from withdrawable funds and label MOCK funding; do not manufacture job earnings or dashboard totals.

Title: Use capability-controlled wallet actions
User story: As a Provider, I want only enabled funding/payout actions so that I do not attempt unavailable financial operations.
Acceptance criteria: Read shared payment capabilities on entry/resume; do not expose Admin gateway settings; handle disabled/unconfigured gateway and conflicts without claiming a completed real transaction.

Title: Set up a supported bank method and withdrawal
User story: As a Provider, I want to initiate supported withdrawals so that available wallet funds can be requested through an eligible method.
Acceptance criteria: Use documented owned payment-method setup/list and withdrawal intent/idempotency contracts; display VERIFIED_MOCK and test outcomes honestly; never imply real bank payout while only MOCK/unconfigured PAYHERE exists.

Title: Recheck payment outcome and reconciliation
User story: As a Provider, I want reliable financial status after interruptions so that I do not repeat a withdrawal or trust an unbalanced wallet.
Acceptance criteria: Retain intentId/idempotency key across retries and fetch authoritative outcome; distinguish pending/succeeded/failed and supported refund cases; block further actions on failed reconciliation and require backend handling.

Title: Receive production earnings settlement
User story: As a Provider, I want completed work settled through a verified payout process so that I receive actual earnings.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm finance approval, earnings release, fee/distribution and real gateway/bank contracts; Customer PAID/RESERVED is not Provider settlement; no mobile client can approve finance or synthesize settlement.

Title: Keep Customer and Provider accounts separated
User story: As an app user, I want the correct role and app identity enforced so that I do not enter the wrong experience or access another role's data.
Acceptance criteria: Preserve distinct native app IDs/display names and role guards; validate restored and newly authenticated roles; never infer role from the launcher icon or a locally edited value.

Title: Keep credentials and diagnostics private
User story: As an app user, I want credentials and personal uploads protected so that debugging and storage do not expose them.
Acceptance criteria: Keep tokens in secure storage and Provider drafts encrypted; exclude secrets/private image URLs from logs; public image hosts never receive app Authorization; preserve correct account scoping and safe error mapping.

Title: Recover from slow or failed requests
User story: As an app user, I want clear loading and retry behavior so that I understand problems without losing my valid work.
Acceptance criteria: Use shared accessible loading/error components where applicable; keep empty data distinct from transport failure; preserve feature drafts and verify coverage again as planned screens are added.

Title: Avoid duplicate or stale actions
User story: As an app user, I want repeated taps and delayed responses handled safely so that the app does not submit duplicates or show another selection's data.
Acceptance criteria: Guard duplicate in-flight writes and ignore replaced/disposed/account-scoped results; use only documented idempotency/read-back recovery; extend lifecycle tests to future booking/payment/job flows.

Title: Use the app with accessible text and motion
User story: As an app user, I want readable scaling, clear semantics and reduced-motion support so that I can complete tasks comfortably.
Acceptance criteria: Support screen-reader labels, keyboard/focus, safe areas and large-text scrolling; expose validation and busy states; reduce success animation motion when requested; audit new workflows on real devices before release.

Title: Understand market time and money
User story: As a Customer or Provider, I want times and currency interpreted consistently so that appointments and financial values are not misleading.
Acceptance criteria: Use returned market timezone/currency, required timestamp formats and decimal-safe money; never derive them from device locale; verify both apps across timezones and changing markets as booking/payment code is added.

Title: Receive meaningful notifications
User story: As a Customer or Provider, I want verified notifications and unread counts so that I can respond to important account or service events.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm feed/read-count/push registration and event contracts plus opt-in behavior; no fabricated counts or silent assumptions of real-time approval; keep unsupported actions disabled or explanatory.

Title: Access support and legal/security actions
User story: As an app user, I want approved support, privacy and account-security destinations so that I can find help and understand my account choices.
Acceptance criteria: Replace disabled links/local guidance only with approved URLs or confirmed APIs; define password change/account deletion/contact support separately; do not create invented destinations or imply a nonfunctional control works.

Title: Preserve routes without bypassing prerequisites
User story: As an app user, I want navigation and returning links to respect my current account state so that I can resume safely.
Acceptance criteria: Keep current auth/onboarding guards and tab routes; invalid IDs/unknown state fail safely; add return-destination support for Customer requirements and future jobs without bypassing account/profile/eligibility checks.

Title: Trust the released app on actual devices
User story: As an app user, I want verified deployed integrations so that tested screens also work with real account data and native capabilities.
Acceptance criteria: Validate live authentication/SMS, public/private media, maps/permissions and configured payment capabilities; run relevant workspace analysis/tests/builds and native smoke tests; do not equate a passing mock test/debug APK with production acceptance.

Title: Customer reviews and ratings submission
User story: As a Customer, I want to review eligible completed care so that future customers can make informed choices.
Acceptance criteria: Define who can review, moderation, visibility and create/edit contracts; keep existing returned rating displays separate from the ability to submit a review.

Title: Favorites and repeat bookings
User story: As a Customer, I want to save preferred providers and reuse past selections so that arranging future care is easier.
Acceptance criteria: Define persistence/privacy and repeat-booking behavior; every new booking must recheck current options, eligibility and availability rather than reuse old approval or prices.

Title: Customer/Provider live coordination
User story: As a Customer or Provider, I want approved real-time communication or tracking so that I can coordinate a live care appointment.
Acceptance criteria: Separately define chat, live location consent, event infrastructure and retention; current approximate service pins/liveTrackingSupported false must never be relabeled as real-time tracking or ETA.

Title: Disputes, cancellations and refunds
User story: As a Customer or Provider, I want an auditable resolution process so that cancellations or service/payment disputes can be handled fairly.
Acceptance criteria: Define product rules, authorized roles, evidence, state transitions and finance integration; current mock refund events do not establish a general cancellation/dispute/refund capability.

Title: Automatic matching and quotes
User story: As a Customer, I want a supported open request or quote workflow so that suitable providers can respond to my needs.
Acceptance criteria: Confirm dispatch/offer/quote lifecycle, provider consent and pricing authority; configured OPEN_REQUEST values alone do not authorize inventing automatic acceptance, quotes or reservations.
